text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London closed lower following a late sell-off in New York. Sentiment was undermined by a build-up in certified coffee stocks in the United States, continued mild weather in Brazil's coffee belt and a reaffirmation by the USDA of a 28 million bag 1997/98 Brazil coffee crop. July lost $65 to close at $1,704 per tonne, while September gave up $54 to close at $1,771 per tonne.

As in London, arabica futures in New York tumbled on statements by the USDA that they stand behind their estimate of 28 million bags of coffee for Brazil. An Attache Report, dated May 9, had put Brazil's 1997/98 harvest at 24 million bags, down sharply from the USDA's official Brazilian estimate of 28 million bags published in its 1997/98 world coffee production report in June. USDA said the lower estimate by the US agricultural Attache did not take into account all factors influencing the crop such as weather, statistical trends and trees planted. Merrill Lynch said in its latest market report that it is difficult to understand why the market took this news so badly. 'First off the market did not slide 15 cents when the USDA report was first released. MEXICO - Mexico is targeting coffee output of 6 mn 60-kg bags for 1997/98 (October/September), up from 5.1 million bags produced the previous year, the Mexican Coffee Council said. It was added that exports should reach 5 million bags in 1996/97 compared to about 4.13 million bags as of the end of June. The Council said that the goal is to increase production by 1 million bags each year until 2000, and let it stabilize at 8 million bags.

UNITED STATES - US certified coffee stocks rose by 4,321 bags as of July 9 to reach 66,115 bags, up from 61,794 bags the previous day and 55,369 bags on July 7. There were 31,959 bags pending grading and the question is, how much of that is 'garbage' coffee being thrown at the board and not likely to pass certification.

POLAND ** - Poland imported 130,258 bags of coffee in March 1997, 13 per cent less than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1997 up to 415,900 bags, slightly less than the 421,000 bags imported the same period in 1996. Total imports in calendar year 1996 rose by nearly 6 per cent to 1.624 million bags. Major suppliers of green coffee in January/March 1997 were Uganda (68,200 vs 13,700 bags), Indonesia (102,200 vs 82,100 bags) and Vietnam (66,700 vs 74,000 bags).

Exports in January/March 1997 reached 22,700 bags, up from 18,400 bags exported the same period in 1996. Total exports in calendar year 1996 reached 88,200 bags, up from 42,300 bags exported the previous year.
SLOVAKIA ** - Slovakia imported 89,300 bags of coffee in January/April 1997. Main suppliers of green coffee were Honduras (12,700 bags) and India (17,500 bags).
